tagline.text: A memorial park on Talisay hill where Rizal spent four years in exile

location.label: Location
location.text: Barangay Talisay, Dapitan City, Zamboanga del Norte (about 1–2 km northwest of the town center)

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: December–May dry season (the July Kinabayo Festival is also good)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,000–3,500 (one day, covering local transport, meals and small entry fees, airfare not included)

children.text: The Dapitan Rizal Shrine is a memorial park on Talisay hill where the Philippine national hero José Rizal lived in exile from 1892 to 1896, building a house and opening a school and a clinic. You can walk to the octagonal Casa Redonda, the waterworks and dam, and the Rizaliana Museum, and adding the Relief Map of Mindanao and the landing site in town makes a half-day outing.

The Dapitan Rizal Shrine (officially the Jose Rizal Memorial Protected Landscape) is in Barangay Talisay, Dapitan City, at the northern tip of the Zamboanga Peninsula. It is a low, peninsula-like hill overlooking Dapitan Bay, about 1–2 km northwest of the town center. According to Wikipedia the protected area covers about 439 hectares, which is large, but the part visitors walk is a section of forest path running from the entrance toward the sea. José Rizal was exiled to this town by the Spanish colonial authorities and stayed nearly four years, from 1892 to 1896. During that time he built his own house, a school, a clinic and a waterworks on this hill.

About two months after arriving in Dapitan, Rizal is said to have won a lottery and used part of the prize to buy about 16 hectares of land for 4,000 pesos, and around March 1893 he moved here to live with his family. As an eye doctor he treated poor patients free of charge, and he is also said to have run a school for boys. The waterworks, reservoir and dam are likewise described as his work. After he left for Manila in 1896 and was executed the following year, the Spanish government seized the land, and when it became a park in 1913, the buildings Rizal had built were reconstructed on their original sites.

On September 3, 1940, the site became Rizal National Park (initially 10 hectares) under Proclamation No. 616 signed by President Quezon. The Rizaliana Museum opened in 1971, the Rizal National Shrine was declared under Presidential Decree No. 105 in 1973, and on April 23, 2000 the area was enlarged and became a protected landscape under Proclamation No. 279. The shrine is described as managed by the National Historical Commission of the Philippines (NHCP), and there are also reports of a separate protected-area office checkpoint on the approach road, so check the notices at the entrance.

The shrine is a place to walk quietly and follow one man's daily life. The octagonal house Casa Redonda, near the entrance, is the first thing you see, and along the forest path come the main house Casa Residencia, the square workshop Casa Cuadrada, the small huts for patients called Casitas de Salud, and the open-air kitchen. On the large rock Mi Retiro, Rizal is said to have written the poems "Mi Retiro" and "Himno a Talisay." Back in town, his traces continue in the Relief Map of Mindanao at the town plaza, St. James Church and the landing place where Rizal came ashore, so in half a day you can follow his four years.

Casa Redonda, the first building you see at the shrine entrance, is an octagonal house on stilts that is said to have housed students and also served as a clinic. Further along the forest path, the main house Casa Residencia, the workshop Casa Cuadrada and the small hexagonal Casa Redonda that served as a henhouse sit close together, so you can see them in 10–20 minutes on foot. They are reconstructed buildings, and today you can look inside and imagine daily life of that time.

The museum, opened in 1971, displays mementos such as the blackboard and table Rizal used when teaching. It is near the entrance and shares a building with the curator's office. Opening days vary by source and many guides list Monday as closed, so if you want to see the museum, aim for Tuesday to Sunday.

Rizal is described as having built the waterworks, dam and reservoir himself. Traces remain today and show the practical side of this doctor and educator. The forest path is slippery when wet, so wear walking shoes.

blocks.title: Mi Retiro rock and sea view

children.text: The large rock in the shrine is known as the spot where Rizal is said to have written the poems "Mi Retiro" and "Himno a Talisay." It looks down on Dapitan Bay and is a good place to sit quietly in the morning or late afternoon light.

blocks.title: Casitas de Salud and the open-air kitchen

children.text: The Casitas de Salud are two small huts that housed male and female patients from distant areas separately. Next to them, the open-air kitchen (cocina) has no walls, only a thatched roof, hinting at the simple life Rizal led while caring for patients.

Near Father Sanchez Street in downtown Dapitan is a giant relief map of the island of Mindanao said to have been made by Rizal. Some visitors say its outline is best seen from the church bell tower, but you need to check whether the tower is open.

blocks.title: St. James Church and Rizal's landing site

children.text: St. James the Greater Church, built in 1871, is described as the church where Rizal attended Mass. The Rizal landing site (Punto del Desembarco) on Sunset Boulevard is where he first stepped ashore in exile; it is free, and people gather there to watch the sea at dusk.

blocks.title: Ilihan Hill and the town plaza

children.text: Ilihan Hill, reached by more than 200 steps from Maria Uray Lane behind the church, was described in past guides as costing about ₱5 and is a good place to look over the town and sea around 4 p.m. The town-center Liwasan ng Dapitan plaza is also described as having been beautified with Rizal's help during his exile.

items.title: Half-day route
items.subtitle: Shrine, then the town's relief map and church, then sunset at the landing site

children.text: Take a tricycle to the Talisay shrine entrance and start with Casa Redonda. You can hire a guide at the entrance for a tip.
Follow the forest path past Casa Residencia, Casa Cuadrada, the Casitas de Salud and the waterworks.
See the mementos and exhibits at the Rizaliana Museum. Check beforehand which day it is closed.
Return to town for lunch.
See the Relief Map of Mindanao and St. James Church.
Climb Ilihan Hill and look over the town and the sea.
Finish with the sunset at the Rizal landing site and Sunset Boulevard.
Shrine opening hours are given as 8 a.m. to 4, 5 or 6 p.m. depending on the source, so going early in the morning is safest.
Land at Dipolog Airport, travel to Dapitan and leave your bags at your lodging.
Follow the half-day route to see the shrine and the town's sights.
Watch the sunset on Sunset Boulevard and have dinner at a restaurant in town.

Enjoy the sea at Dakak Park and Beach Resort or make a day visit. Guides disagree on the day-visit fee, from about ₱500 per person (2021) to ₱1,000 (2015, 2017 and 2023 guides), so check the current price.
Go to Dipolog for a flight to Manila, or cross to Dumaguete by ferry.

1 hour 20 minutes–1 hour 45 minutes

Operators and times are described differently by different sources, and fares are given at roughly

The Talisay shrine is about

from the town center and easy to reach by tricycle. Tricycle fares in town are very low, but confirm the price before you ride.
In your map app, search for "Rizal Shrine Dapitan" or "Jose Rizal Memorial Protected Landscape."
The shrine involves a lot of outdoor walking on forest paths, so the less rainy dry season is the most comfortable. Generally
December–May
is clear and good for walking, and to avoid the midday heat, visit in the early morning or late afternoon.
From
July 16–31
the Kinabayo Festival honors the city's patron saint, St. James (July 25), and the city is lively. In the
June–November
rainy season, rain and downpours make the forest path slippery, and on rainy days it is better to switch to the museum and the church.

Small guesthouses and pension houses cluster in downtown Dapitan and near Sunset Boulevard. Wikivoyage lists Travelbee Heritage Inn Dapitan from ₱1,100 and Monina Pension House at ₱500–700, but prices may be out of date, so confirm before booking. If you want time by the sea, Dakak Park and Beach Resort in Taguilon is the best-known choice.

Meals are found at downtown restaurants and seaside stalls. Being a coastal city, fresh grilled fish and seafood are common, and Kamayan ni Manay is mentioned as a long-running home-style restaurant. Opening hours and menus change, so check on site.
The museum is sometimes closed on Mondays, so plan to go Tuesday to Sunday; the shrine opens at 8 a.m. but closing times differ between sources, so arrive before 4 p.m.
Hiring a guide at the shrine entrance for a tip lets you hear Rizal's story and understand the buildings more easily.
There is a lot of forest path, so bring comfortable walking shoes, a hat, water and insect repellent.
In the rainy season the forest path gets slippery in downpours and photos are hard to take, so see the shrine first in the morning.
Entrance fees and opening hours differ between sources. Check the NHCP or Dapitan city tourism information before your visit.
You will enjoy the visit much more with some background on Rizal's life, so read a short biography before you go.
Lodging fills up quickly during the July Kinabayo Festival, so book ahead.
Entrance fees and opening hours differ by source, so confirm them locally before your visit.
There are reports that the protected-area checkpoint at the entrance has charged fees in the past, so ask for a receipt and confirm the amount.
Museum closing days and hours may change.
The forest path and areas around the waterworks are slippery in the rainy season and have many mosquitoes, so be careful.
Ferry times differ greatly by operator and sailings can be cancelled by weather, so leave plenty of slack in your schedule.
Do not touch or write on the reconstructed buildings and exhibits.

Built in 1871 and described as the church where Rizal attended Mass. It is in the town center and reachable on foot.
